hero.label: About us
hero.title: We started after the 2015 earthquake, and we kept going
hero.text: Tulsi Heera Foundation helps children in Nepal stay in school when their families cannot pay for it.

paragraphs.p1: In 2015 a huge earthquake hit Nepal. Sindhupalchowk was one of the worst-hit districts. We collected some money and went to visit the villages around Chautara.
paragraphs.p2: We met many children who had lost their families and were now living with relatives. Some of these relatives were so poor that the children were not going to school, even though a year at a government school cost only about 3,000 rupees at the time.
paragraphs.p3: The money we had collected was not much, so we decided to use it for what mattered most: paying for these children to go to school.
paragraphs.p4: At first we helped only children affected by the earthquake. Then the village leaders in Chautara and the school headmaster told us that many organisations were already helping earthquake victims, while other poor and orphaned children were getting no help at all.
paragraphs.p5: So we changed. Since then we have supported any child who needs help to stay in school, whether or not the earthquake affected them.

hero.label: Our work
hero.title: Paying for a child's school year
hero.text: Our main work is simple: we pay school fees for children who would otherwise have to stop going to school.

paragraphs.p1: Many children in Sindhupalchowk have lost one or both parents. Others live with families who cannot afford the yearly school fees.
paragraphs.p2: We pay those fees so the children can stay in school. We have done this every year since 2015.

hero.title: Privacy and cookies
hero.text: In short: this website uses no cookies, does not track you and has no forms. We only get your details if you call us or message us.

whoWeAre.title: Who runs this website
whoWeAre.text: This website belongs to the Tulsi Heera Foundation, based in Kathmandu, Nepal. If you have a question about your information, call us or message us on WhatsApp using the contact details at the bottom of this page.

cookies.title: Cookies
cookies.text: This website does not use cookies and does not save anything on your device. We do not use analytics, advertising or any other tracking. That is why you do not see a cookie banner.

videos.title: Videos from YouTube
videos.text: The videos on our Stories page are hosted on YouTube, which belongs to Google. A video does not load until you press play. Once you do, YouTube receives your IP address and may save cookies on your device, under Google's own privacy policy.

contact.title: When you call or message us
contact.text: If you call us or message us on WhatsApp, we see your phone number and anything you choose to tell us, such as your name. We use it only to answer you, arrange your donation and send your donation certificate. We do not sell it, and we only share it if the law requires us to. WhatsApp is run by Meta, which has its own privacy policy.

supporters.title: Our supporters' names
supporters.text: To thank them, we list some of our supporters by name. If you are on the list and want your name removed, or want it added, tell us and we will change it.

children.title: Children in our stories
children.text: We use only the first names of the children in our stories. If you are a parent or guardian and want a story changed or removed, contact us.

hosting.title: Website hosting
hosting.text: Like all websites, ours runs on a hosting provider's servers. These may keep basic technical logs, such as IP addresses and the pages visited, to keep the site working and safe. We do not use these logs to identify you.

rights.title: Your rights
rights.text: You can ask us what information we have about you, and ask us to correct it or delete it. If you live in the European Union, you can also complain to your data protection authority. In Spain, this is the AEPD (Spanish Data Protection Agency).
